title: Eddington's 1919 eclipse expedition
summary: During the total solar eclipse of 29 May 1919, British teams photographed stars near the Sun at Príncipe, led by Arthur Eddington, and at Sobral in Brazil. Measured deflections were 1.61 ± 0.30 arcseconds at Príncipe and 1.98 ± 0.12 with Sobral's 4-inch telescope, against 1.75 for relativity and 0.87 for Newtonian gravity.

as_recorded.value: May 29, 1919, during a total solar eclipse

where.modern_name: Roça Sundy, Príncipe, São Tomé and Príncipe (a second team observed at Sobral, Ceará, Brazil)
where.historical_name: Roça Sundy plantation, Príncipe island, Portuguese territory off the West African coast

importance.justification: The measurements were reported as confirming the relativity prediction at a joint Royal Society and RAS session on 6 November 1919.

reviewer_note: The record pins Eddington's Príncipe site (Roça Sundy per the Frankfurt page; FAPESP does not name it). Sobral could be added as a second region (OSM: -3.8565, -40.0439). Frankfurt gives the Príncipe result as 1.7 arcseconds while FAPESP gives 1.61 ± 0.30; the summary uses FAPESP. Sources mention later disputes over discarded Sobral plates.
